name: Speed Limits
description: Establishing reduced speed limitations on residential and commercial streets citywide.
summary: The contested/citywide discussion centered on whether stop signs and speed-control measures on residential streets comply with MUTCD warrants, with a speaker at the 2026-06-09 Committee on Pedestrian and Traffic Safety meeting urging the committee to stop approving unwarranted residential stop-sign control based on CDOT boilerplate [2]. Committee discussion on 2026-02-09 covered citywide Complete Streets, Neighborhood Greenways with typical 20 mph limits on residential streets, and safety work on arterial/commercial corridors [1], while public comment raised concerns about speeding, speed cameras, and enforcement [3]. The specific decisions were street-level 20 mph speed-limit ordinances: twelve measures (e.g., O2026-0024946 introduced 2026-04-15, and O2026-0025966 through O2026-0025988 introduced 2026-06-09) passed City Council 49 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-06-17, and three more (O2026-0026630, O2026-0026640, O2026-0026642, introduced 2026-07-07) passed 49 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-07-15. Agendas for the 2026-06-09 and 2026-07-07 committee meetings list these speed limitations as direct introductions [9][10][11][12]. Still open is any broader citywide reduced-speed policy: at the 2026-10-09 committee, a member expressed support for citywide measures but sought CDOT coordination on business-district design [5], and no citywide speed-limit ordinance appears in the record trail.
one_line: Street-level 20 mph speed limits passed 49-0; citywide residential speed policy and stop-sign warrant compliance remain unresolved.
